image.layers: ubuntu:24.04 (digest-pinned) + runtime apt (python3, the QEMU fork's libs, falcon/gunicorn) + /opt/esp: ESP-IDF v5.5.5 431 MB (no .git/examples/docs) + tools 862 MB (riscv32-esp-elf with ONE multilib, rv32imc_zicsr_zifencei/ilp32; picolibc dropped: 2050 → ~660 MB) + python env 92 MB
image.why_not_espressif_idf: every target installed: 5 116 MB compressed (Docker Hub, amd64, 2026-10-02), > 12 GB unpacked — more than this device had free

build.source: polari-idf-build wait4 on idf.py build, a from-scratch build of c3-prio-inversion (2 runs: 56.9 / 57.1 s; c3-sim-rig 56.6 s); size 0.95 s, merge_bin 0.09 s; the build is REPRODUCIBLE (CONFIG_APP_REPRODUCIBLE_BUILD: the same image sha256 across runs and across the image and worker rungs)

twin.scenario_run_wall_s: 0.3-0.9 s per scenario run inside QEMU (boot + window, -icount 3, sleep=off); ~1.5 s per run end to end through docker run
twin.source: board.custom.sim_cost_c3 on c3-prio-inversion (3 runs: 0.533 / 0.534 / 0.533); twin mode (-icount shift=auto,sleep=on): virtual/wall settles at 0.7-1.1 after a burst of ~35 virtual s in the first ~2 wall s

image_build.note: docker build --no-cache with the digest-pinned base already local (2026-10-02): apt 110 s, the ESP-IDF shallow recursive clone 86 s, idf_tools (toolchain, QEMU, cmake, ninja) + the python env 154 s, the prune 6 s, the /opt/esp copy into the runtime stage 57 s, export 28 s; network-bound
